items.title: Live Updates: Investigators Seek to Establish Motive in FlyDubai Attack
items.summary: The United Arab Emirates said it would lead the investigation, including into possible links to terrorism. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the attacker had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination,” though he did not elaborate.

items.title: Russia to Sharply Increase War Spending and Cut Social Programs
items.summary: Both sides are finding it increasingly difficult to finance the conflict in Ukraine. Russia’s 2027 budget envisions more debt, higher taxes and lower social benefits.

items.title: Finnish Lawmakers Report Suspicious Home Break-Ins
items.summary: The speaker of Parliament said there were a “considerable” number of mysterious entries in which perpetrators appeared to have taken nothing.

items.title: A Flashy Zimbabwean Tycoon Who Befriended Presidents Dies in Crash
items.summary: Wicknell Chivayo was riding in a helicopter with his wife when it plunged into a field. Dogged by corruption allegations, the businessman drew polarizing reactions even in death.

items.title: Who Is Captain Smit Machchhar, the Pilot Hailed as a Hero After FlyDubai Cockpit Stabbing?
items.summary: Capt. Smit Machchhar suffered stab wounds while fending off an attack from his co-pilot, saving the lives of around 170 people on board, officials said.

items.title: One Issue Hanging Over Brazil’s Presidential Election: Online Gambling and Record-High Debts
items.summary: Just days before Sunday’s election, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva banned online gambling. But record-high debt is upending millions of lives.

items.title: Take a Historic Stroll Down Oxford Street, London’s Shopping Artery
items.summary: London is making a stretch of the street, long central to the city’s identity and sense of style, car free.

items.title: Swiss Glaciers Vanished by Nearly a Fifth in Recent Years, Scientists Say
items.summary: One researcher called it a “desperately needed warning sign” that countries need to tackle human-driven climate change.

items.title: Britain and France Give Up Landmark Migrant Agreement
items.summary: The French government soured on a reciprocal deal that allowed the British authorities to return some migrants who crossed the English Channel illegally in small boats.

items.title: Hong Kong Journalist Arrested After Covering Gathering Linked to 2019 Protests
items.summary: The national security police detained Tang Ho-wing, founder of the independent outlet Boom News, according to local media and watchdog groups.

items.title: Most American Children Are Being Auto-Enrolled in Trump Accounts. What to Know.

items.title: As Mortgage Rates Hit Highest Level Since 2023, Buyers Look at ARMs
items.summary: The average 30-year, fixed-rate home loan rose to 7.28 percent, up from 6.34 percent a year ago. More buyers are now turning to adjustable-rate mortgages.

items.title: Trump’s Threat to Ban Diesel Exports Sets Off Global Alarms
items.summary: A reduction in refineries has already driven the price of diesel to record highs, threatening economies. An U.S. export ban would be “tremendous shock and blow.”

items.title: Federal Watchdog Investigates Adam Kinzinger for Kalshi Bets on His Pardon
items.summary: The inquiry by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission centers on bets the former congressman made on Kalshi in the weeks before he was pardoned in January 2025.

items.title: U.S. Bond Yields Hit Highest Level Since 2002
items.summary: The factors pushing up yields, including the war in Iran and high government debt levels, are unlikely to dissipate soon.

items.title: The Global Bond Rout Reaches Worrying New Levels
items.summary: Investors are on alert as the yield on the 10-year Treasury note hit a new multi-decade high. The sell-off is also broadening in Europe, too.

items.title: Oil Is Flowing From the Persian Gulf, but Prices Remain High. Why?
items.summary: Crude oil costs close to $100 a barrel because traders are worried hostilities could soon restart and the world is burning through its emergency stockpiles.

items.title: How Middle East Oil Exports Started Recovering
items.summary: Our business reporter Peter Eavis describes how oil exports from the Middle East have rebounded this month, getting closer to the levels seen before the Iran war.

items.title: When Data Centers Cluster Together, How Dirty Are They? One County Wants Answers.

items.title: Inside Binance Founder Changpeng Zhao’s Life After Prison
items.summary: Changpeng Zhao, jailed in the United States for a financial crime and pardoned by President Trump, is now living a gilded life in the United Arab Emirates.
